name: Question 9
problem:
Consider the vector space ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$ of all $2\times 2$ matrices over $R.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]}$ is a linearly independent set in ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
- $[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]}$
- ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

is true if and only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ So, the set is linearly independent.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]=(-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+(-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

- Statement III is false. For example, the matrix $[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ can't be written as a linear combination of 

$$
{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]}
$$

since all these linear combinations result in matrices with the entry ${a}_{22}=0:$

$$
a\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+b\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+c\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a & 6b \\ -2c & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

Question 9
?

Consider the vector space M2(R) of all 2×2 matrices over R.

Which of the following statements are true?

  1. {[1000],[0600],[00−20]} is a linearly independent set in M2(R)
  2. [−1320] can be expressed as a linear combination of {[1000],[0600],[00−20]}
  3. {[1000],[0600],[00−20]} is a basis of M2(R)
a
II only
b
I, II, and III
c
I and III only
d
I and II only
e
II and III only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation x1⋅[1000]+x2⋅[0600]+x3⋅[00−20]=[0000] is true if and only if x1=x2=x3=0. So, the set is linearly independent.

  • Statement II is true. Indeed, [−1320]=(−1)⋅[1000]+12⋅[0600]+(−1)⋅[00−20].

  • Statement III is false. For example, the matrix [1111] can't be written as a linear combination of {[1000],[0600],[00−20]} since all these linear combinations result in matrices with the entry a22=0: a⋅[1000]+b⋅[0600]+c⋅[00−20]=[a6b−2c0]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
